enonce_markdown: The vectors $\mathbf{p}=2\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}-2\mathbf{k}$ and $\mathbf{q}=\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j}+2\mathbf{k}$ are drawn from the same point. The angle between them, to the nearest $0.1^\circ$, is
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The scalar product can be computed in components, $\mathbf{p}\cdot\mathbf{q}=p_1q_1+p_2q_2+p_3q_3$, and also equals $|\mathbf{p}||\mathbf{q}|\cos\theta$. Equating the two gives $\cos\theta$; a negative value means the angle is obtuse.

### Solution

$\mathbf{p}\cdot\mathbf{q}=(2)(1)+(1)(-2)+(-2)(2)=-4$.

$|\mathbf{p}|=\sqrt{4+1+4}=3$ and $|\mathbf{q}|=\sqrt{1+4+4}=3$.

$$\cos\theta=\frac{-4}{3\times 3}=-\frac{4}{9}\quad\Rightarrow\quad \theta=\cos^{-1}\!\left(-\tfrac49\right)\approx 116.4^\circ.$$

The angle is obtuse because the scalar product is negative. The value $63.6^\circ$ comes from dropping the minus sign, $26.4^\circ$ from using $\sin^{-1}$ instead of $\cos^{-1}$, and $153.6^\circ$ is $180^\circ-26.4^\circ$. **Answer: c.**

enonce_markdown: Given $\mathbf{a}=2\mathbf{i}-\mathbf{j}+3\mathbf{k}$ and $\mathbf{b}=\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j}-\mathbf{k}$, the vector product $\mathbf{a}\times\mathbf{b}$ is
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Expand $\mathbf{a}\times\mathbf{b}$ as a determinant whose rows are $\mathbf{i},\mathbf{j},\mathbf{k}$, then the components of $\mathbf{a}$, then those of $\mathbf{b}$. The $\mathbf{j}$ term carries a minus sign, and swapping the order of the factors reverses the whole vector.

### Solution

$$\mathbf{a}\times\mathbf{b}=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf{i}&\mathbf{j}&\mathbf{k}\\ 2&-1&3\\ 1&4&-1\end{vmatrix}
=\big((-1)(-1)-(3)(4)\big)\mathbf{i}-\big((2)(-1)-(3)(1)\big)\mathbf{j}+\big((2)(4)-(-1)(1)\big)\mathbf{k}$$

$$=-11\mathbf{i}+5\mathbf{j}+9\mathbf{k}.$$

Check: the result is perpendicular to both vectors, since $(-11)(2)+(5)(-1)+(9)(3)=0$ and $(-11)(1)+(5)(4)+(9)(-1)=0$.

The option $11\mathbf{i}-5\mathbf{j}-9\mathbf{k}$ is $\mathbf{b}\times\mathbf{a}$, the option with $-5\mathbf{j}$ forgets the minus sign of the $\mathbf{j}$ term, and $2\mathbf{i}-4\mathbf{j}-3\mathbf{k}$ multiplies the components one by one (which is not a vector product). **Answer: d.**

enonce_markdown: Let $\mathbf{u}$ have components $(\lambda,\,2,\,-1)$ and $\mathbf{v}$ have components $(3,\,\lambda,\,4)$, where $\lambda$ is a constant. If $\mathbf{u}$ is perpendicular to $\mathbf{v}$, then $\lambda$ equals
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Two non-zero vectors are perpendicular exactly when their scalar product is zero. Write $\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}$ in components, keep every sign, and solve the resulting linear equation for $\lambda$.

### Solution

$$\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}=(\lambda)(3)+(2)(\lambda)+(-1)(4)=5\lambda-4=0\quad\Rightarrow\quad\lambda=\frac45.$$

Check: with $\lambda=\tfrac45$, $\tfrac{12}{5}+\tfrac{8}{5}-4=0$.

The value $\tfrac43$ comes from forgetting the term $2\lambda$, the value $4$ from a sign slip ($3\lambda-2\lambda-4=0$), and $\tfrac54$ from inverting the fraction. **Answer: a.**

enonce_markdown: The points $A(1,0,2)$, $B(3,1,1)$ and $C(2,3,4)$ are the vertices of a triangle. Find the exact area of triangle $ABC$.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The magnitude of a vector product is $|\mathbf{a}\times\mathbf{b}|=|\mathbf{a}||\mathbf{b}|\sin\theta$, which is the area of the parallelogram on $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$. The triangle has half this area: $\tfrac12|\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AC}|$.

### Solution

**Two sides from $A$.**

$$\overrightarrow{AB}=(3-1,\,1-0,\,1-2)=2\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}-\mathbf{k},\qquad \overrightarrow{AC}=(2-1,\,3-0,\,4-2)=\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}+2\mathbf{k}.$$

**Vector product.**

$$\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AC}=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf{i}&\mathbf{j}&\mathbf{k}\\ 2&1&-1\\ 1&3&2\end{vmatrix}
=(2+3)\mathbf{i}-(4+1)\mathbf{j}+(6-1)\mathbf{k}=5\mathbf{i}-5\mathbf{j}+5\mathbf{k}.$$

**Area.**

$$\left|\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AC}\right|=\sqrt{25+25+25}=5\sqrt3,\qquad \text{Area}=\frac12\times5\sqrt3=\frac{5\sqrt3}{2}\approx 4.33.$$

$$\boxed{\text{Area}=\dfrac{5\sqrt3}{2}}$$

enonce_markdown:
A crane at Douala port pulls a load with a constant force $\mathbf{F}=(4\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j}+5\mathbf{k})$ N, moving it from the point $A(1,2,0)$ to the point $B(4,0,3)$, where distances are in metres.

(a) Find the work done by the force.

(b) Find the component of $\mathbf{F}$ in the direction of $\overrightarrow{AB}$, giving your answer to three significant figures.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

For a constant force, work done is the scalar product of the force and the displacement, $W=\mathbf{F}\cdot\mathbf{s}$. The component of $\mathbf{F}$ along a direction is $\mathbf{F}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{s}}$, where $\hat{\mathbf{s}}=\mathbf{s}/|\mathbf{s}|$ is the unit vector in that direction.

### Solution

**(a)** The displacement is $\mathbf{s}=\overrightarrow{AB}=(4-1)\mathbf{i}+(0-2)\mathbf{j}+(3-0)\mathbf{k}=3\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j}+3\mathbf{k}$ (metres).

$$W=\mathbf{F}\cdot\mathbf{s}=(4)(3)+(-2)(-2)+(5)(3)=12+4+15=31\ \text{J}.$$

**(b)** $|\mathbf{s}|=\sqrt{9+4+9}=\sqrt{22}$, so the component of $\mathbf{F}$ along $\overrightarrow{AB}$ is

$$\frac{\mathbf{F}\cdot\mathbf{s}}{|\mathbf{s}|}=\frac{31}{\sqrt{22}}\approx 6.61\ \text{N}.$$

(Consistency check: work $=$ component $\times$ distance $=\dfrac{31}{\sqrt{22}}\times\sqrt{22}=31$ J.)

$$\boxed{W=31\ \text{J},\qquad \text{component}\approx 6.61\ \text{N}}$$

enonce_markdown: A straight line $l$ has vector equation $\mathbf{r}=\mathbf{i}-\mathbf{k}+t\,(2\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}+2\mathbf{k})$, where $t$ is a real parameter, and $P$ is the point with position vector $\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j}+3\mathbf{k}$. The shortest distance from $P$ to $l$ is
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

If $A$ is a point on a line with direction vector $\mathbf{d}$, the perpendicular distance from a point $P$ to the line is $|AP|\sin\theta=\dfrac{|\overrightarrow{AP}\times\mathbf{d}|}{|\mathbf{d}|}$. The scalar product $\dfrac{\overrightarrow{AP}\cdot\mathbf{d}}{|\mathbf{d}|}$ gives instead the length of the projection of $\overrightarrow{AP}$ along the line.

### Solution

Take $A(1,0,-1)$ on the line and $\mathbf{d}=2\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}+2\mathbf{k}$, so $|\mathbf{d}|=\sqrt{4+1+4}=3$.

$$\overrightarrow{AP}=(0,\,2,\,4),\qquad \overrightarrow{AP}\times\mathbf{d}=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf{i}&\mathbf{j}&\mathbf{k}\\ 0&2&4\\ 2&1&2\end{vmatrix}=(4-4)\mathbf{i}-(0-8)\mathbf{j}+(0-4)\mathbf{k}=8\mathbf{j}-4\mathbf{k}.$$

$$|\overrightarrow{AP}\times\mathbf{d}|=\sqrt{64+16}=4\sqrt5,\qquad \text{distance}=\frac{4\sqrt5}{3}\approx 2.98.$$

Check: the foot of the perpendicular is at $t=\tfrac{\overrightarrow{AP}\cdot\mathbf{d}}{|\mathbf{d}|^2}=\tfrac{10}{9}$, and the distance from $P$ to that point is again $\tfrac{4\sqrt5}{3}$.

The option $\tfrac{10}{3}$ is the projection $\overrightarrow{AP}\cdot\mathbf{d}/|\mathbf{d}|$ (scalar product used instead of vector product), $4\sqrt5$ forgets to divide by $|\mathbf{d}|$, and $\tfrac{4\sqrt5}{9}$ divides by $|\mathbf{d}|^2$. **Answer: b.**
